PART I

Item 1. Business

Northwind Logistics provides ground freight, air freight, and warehousing services across North America. We operate 42 distribution centres and a fleet of approximately 3,100 tractors. Our Ground segment is the largest of our three reportable segments by revenue and by headcount.

We were incorporated in Delaware in 1994 and our principal executive offices are located in Columbus, Ohio. Our services are sold through a direct sales force and through a network of freight brokers. Seasonality affects our results, with the fourth quarter historically the strongest.

Competition in freight and logistics is intense and fragmented. We compete on service reliability, network density, and price. Some competitors have greater financial resources than we do.

Item 1A. Risk Factors

A significant portion of our Ground segment revenue is concentrated among a small number of customers. In fiscal 2024, our three largest customers accounted for approximately 28% of consolidated net revenue. The loss of any one of these customers could materially affect our results of operations.

Fuel price volatility affects our operating costs. While most customer contracts contain fuel surcharge provisions, these provisions may lag actual cost increases and may not recover the full amount of any increase.

We depend on the availability of qualified drivers. The market for drivers is competitive and driver shortages have periodically increased our compensation costs and constrained our ability to grow the Ground segment.

Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition

Results of Operations. Total net revenue for fiscal 2024 was $4,218 million, an increase of 11.0% compared with $3,800 million in fiscal 2023. The increase was driven primarily by higher freight volumes in the Ground segment and by contractual rate escalators that took effect in the second quarter.

(1) Warehousing segment revenue for fiscal 2024 includes $31 million of non-recurring termination fees related to the exit of two leased facilities in the Midwest. Excluding these fees, Warehousing revenue grew 4.0%.

Operating expenses increased 9.4% to $3,782 million, below the rate of revenue growth, producing operating margin expansion of 120 basis points. Purchased transportation was the largest single expense category.
